what_happened: On the highway at about 41 m/s, the ego drifted left toward the lane the recorded human moved into, while actor 5 was still in that lane right beside it. The ego's front clipped actor 5. The ego never braked or held its lane while closing on 5.

After taking over at 4.6 s on a straight multi-lane highway, the policy slowed hard from about 35 to 21 m/s and steered left away from the human path, which bore slightly right. By 6.5 s the ego had crossed the left lane edge onto the shoulder or grass, about 5 m off the recording, and following car 7 hit its rear as it braked. The camera view was clean before the drift, and there was no lead vehicle close enough to explain the braking.

After handoff the ego braked hard (20→8 m/s) and veered right off the recorded path, which kept it straight and then left (command LEFT), into the lane of truck 5. Its front struck the left rear side of the truck at 8.1 s. The rear contact and offroad flags came after this collision.

The highway curved left and the route command changed to LEFT, but the ego kept going nearly straight at about 19–21 m/s. It drifted across the right lane edge and off the road into the trees on the right shoulder, ending about 8 m from the human's recorded path. No other actors were involved, and the camera view looked fine until the ego left the road.

At about 16–18 m/s on a curving highway with no lead vehicle, the ego stayed right instead of following the route toward the left lanes (the command changed from STRAIGHT to LEFT). It drifted across the right edge line onto the shoulder and into the vegetation, ending 7 m from the recorded path. The right side of the camera view smears as the ego leaves the recorded path, but this follows the drift rather than causing it.

Right after handoff, on a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT and then LEFT, the policy's planned path bent right and the ego drifted out of the rightmost lane, across the edge line and onto the dirt shoulder at about 6 m/s, ending 3.5 m from the human's path. The camera was clean when it started drifting, and no actor was close (the lead was 45–60 m ahead).

The road curves left (the command changes from STRAIGHT to LEFT), but the ego kept going straight and drifted right out of its lane onto the shoulder, where cars 54 and 58 were parked. It slowed only from 16 to 10 m/s and ran front-first into parked car 54 at 10.2 s, about 15.7 m off the human's path. The camera view was clean before the impact.

The ego was driving straight in the rightmost lane at about 12–13 m/s with no vehicle ahead. Where the road bends gently left, the policy's planned path kept going straight and edged right toward the curb, so the ego's right side went over the road edge at 5.6 s, about 0.7 m from where the human drove.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the ego was already on the right edge of the rightmost lane when the policy took over. Then the command changed to LEFT and the recorded path went left, but the planned path kept curving right, so the ego drifted across the shoulder onto the dirt verge. It was 3.5 m off the recording at 6.3 m/s when the offroad failure was recorded, and the camera view was clear enough that rendering does not explain it.

After handoff the ego was in the rightmost highway lane at about 5–6 m/s. Its planned path bent right across the lane edge onto the dirt shoulder, while the recorded human path stayed in the lane, and the ego ended up offroad about 3.6 m from the recorded path at 7.3 s. The camera view was clean before the drift and no actor was involved.

The ego was going straight at about 13 m/s in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane arterial road with no lead vehicle. Within a second of the policy taking over at 4.6 s, it drifted about 0.7 m right of the recorded path, and its right side crossed the road edge line, so the run was flagged offroad at 5.6 s; the planned path was already curving back left.

Going straight in the rightmost lane at about 12–13 m/s with no lead vehicle, the policy took over at 4.6 s and its planned path (orange) bent right, away from the recorded path (green) and across the right edge line. By 5.6 s the ego box was over the right road boundary and was flagged offroad, only about 0.7 m from where the human drove.

After the policy took over at 4.6s on a straight highway (command STRAIGHT), the ego braked hard from about 35 to 21 m/s and steered left, away from the route. By 6.5s it had crossed the left lanes and left the road onto the median, about 5 m from the recorded path. Because it slowed sharply while veering, the following actor 7 also hit its rear at that moment.

On a straight highway with a RIGHT command, the policy took over at 4.6 s, braked hard from 35 to 21 m/s, and steered left away from the recorded path, which went right. By 6.5 s it had left the left edge of the lanes onto the grass median, about 5 m from the human's path, and a following car (actor 7) hit its rear at the same moment.

On the highway, after taking over, the ego braked hard (21 → 8 m/s) and drifted right across the lane line into the lane of semi-truck 5. Its front hit the truck at about 8.0 s, 4.6 m off the recorded path. The command was STRAIGHT and then LEFT, and the truck was clearly visible in the camera before the impact.

On a curving multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard from 20 to 8 m/s. Instead of following the left-bending lanes as the human did under the LEFT command, it held its heading and drifted right into the lane of semi-truck 5, which was passing on the right. The ego's front hit the side of the truck.

The road curves left and the route command changes to LEFT, but the ego slows from about 23 to 18 m/s while holding a nearly straight heading. It drifts across the right lane line and goes off the right edge toward the trees, about 7.8 m from where the human drove. The camera view was clean before the drift, and there was no actor ahead.

On a road that curves left, the ego kept a nearly straight path and drifted right out of its lane toward the shoulder, where cars 54 and 58 are parked. It braked only slightly (16 to 10 m/s while the gap fell from 43 m to 4 m) and its front hit parked car 54, about 15.6 m from the recorded human path.

On a left-hand curve (command LEFT), the ego didn't follow the curve the way the human did. It held a straighter line into the right edge, where cars 54 and 58 were parked, ending up about 15.6 m off the recorded path. It slowed only from about 15 to 11 m/s while the gap to parked car 54 shrank from 37 m to 4 m, and its front hit that car.

On a left-curving road, the ego drifted right out of its lane onto the shoulder, where cars 54 and 58 were parked. It slowed from about 16 to 10.5 m/s but kept closing on them and hit parked car 54 head-on, about 15.6 m from the recorded human path. The rear contact happened after this front collision.

The road curves left (command LEFT), but the ego kept going straight and moved into the right edge or parking lane, about 15 m off the recorded path. Two parked cars (54 and 58) were in that lane. It closed from 43 m to 4 m on parked car 54 while slowing only from 16 to 10 m/s, and hit it head-on.

On a highway that bends left, the ego stayed in the rightmost lane and kept heading nearly straight while slowing from 26 to 17.5 m/s. It ignored the LEFT command and the planned route, which moved left across the lanes, so it ran off the right edge of the road and ended about 8 m from the human trajectory. The camera view was clean at 7.9 s, and the smearing only shows up once the ego is already off the road.

Driving at about 20–25 m/s on a highway that curves left, the ego held a straight-to-slightly-right heading while its route (command STRAIGHT, then LEFT) bent left. It drifted out of the rightmost lane across the right edge line and left the road at 9.2 s, about 7.6 m from the human's path. No other actors were involved.

The highway curves left (the route command changes from STRAIGHT to LEFT). The ego slowed from 25 to 17 m/s, but its planned path stayed nearly straight instead of following the curve. It drifted across the right lane edge and left the road on the right at 9.1 s, about 7.7 m from the human's path. The camera view was clean before the failure; it only smeared once the ego was in the roadside trees.

On a motorway at about 41 m/s, the ego drifted left toward the lane line next to it while closing on the slower white SUV (actor 5) in the left lane, without braking. Its front-left hit the SUV at 6.9 s. The ego was running about 27 m ahead of the recorded drive and moved left into space the SUV already occupied.

The ego was going about 41 m/s on a multi-lane highway and drifted left toward the next lane, roughly following the logged lane change. Because it never slowed, it was about 27 m ahead of where the human was at that moment. Its front ran into the slower car 5 in the left lane (the gap shrank to 3.4 m) at full speed, with no braking.
